title: Torqex Industrial nameplate mark: triage two captures, prep-and-trace the flat artwork into a clean vector master, and build the K100 / reverse / isolated-bolt / sized-lockup production set
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com logo brief (the original asked for a mark in 'fully editable vector format (.ai or .eps)', 'instantly readable at small sizes' on labels and swing tags, 'print-ready CMYK output and scalable vector artwork', shipped with 'one-colour and reverse variants'). Designing a NEW mark from scratch is out of Adobe-connector scope (no from-scratch letterform/compositional art), so the doable, in-scope reading of that same requirement — take what the client actually has and turn it into clean, scalable, production-ready vector artwork plus the one-colour + reverse variants and sized lockups the brief names — is a VECTORIZE-AND-PRODUCTION-SET job. The vertical is laundered from casual apparel to a fictional IP-clean industrial-equipment brand, Torqex Industrial (maker of hydraulic torque tools; wordmark 'TORQEX' with a hex-bolt / torque-arrow icon and a 'HYDRAULIC TORQUE SYSTEMS' tagline), whose mark gets laser-etched onto anodized-aluminium machine nameplates and screen-printed onto tool cases — the brief's 'small-size readability' and 'one-colour / reverse variants' clauses map cleanly onto that. ENRICHMENT that makes the chain concrete, failable and measurable: the original editable vector was lost, so the client has only two raster captures of the mark that superficially both look like 'the logo' — a flat scan of an old printed artwork proof, and a photograph of the mark already etched on a physical nameplate bolted to a machine. The two captures needing OPPOSITE correct treatments (trace one, isolate the other) is the enrichment that creates the triage; the sizes, the anodized-plate context, and the icon/wordmark structure are reasonable and contradict nothing in the source. Fictional brand and persona; no real trademark, company or proprietary data.
one_line_ask: From two look-alike captures of the Torqex mark — a flat printed-artwork scan and a photo of the mark etched on a machine nameplate — decide which is the trace source, prep it (deskew, drive paper to clean white and ink to solid black, trim, knock to transparency) and vectorize it into a clean vector master, then derive the isolated hex-bolt icon vector, the white reverse lockup, and two sized plate/label lockups from it; the nameplate photo must instead be cleaned and isolated into a catalog product cutout, NOT traced.
full_brief:
Torqex Industrial makes hydraulic torque tools, and we're re-tooling the artwork for our machine nameplates and tool cases. Our brand mark is the 'TORQEX' wordmark next to a hex-bolt / torque-arrow icon, with a small 'HYDRAULIC TORQUE SYSTEMS' tagline. The problem: the original editable vector file is long gone, and all we can find are two pictures of the mark. We need a proper, clean, scalable vector master rebuilt from what we have, plus the full production set our vendors keep asking for.

The two pictures we could dig up:
(1) torqex_artwork_scan.png — a flatbed scan of an old printed artwork proof of the mark (black ink on off-white stock). It went through the scanner slightly crooked, the paper has gone a bit cream/yellow with age and shows paper texture and a faint edge shadow, and the printed mark itself is flat, high-contrast line art.
(2) torqex_plate_photo.jpg — a photo of the same mark as it appears laser-etched into one of our anodized-aluminium machine nameplates, still bolted to the machine. It's shot at a slight angle, the brushed-metal surface throws glare and grain, and there are corner fixing screws and machine housing around it.

Use your own judgement about how to get the best possible result out of each one — that's the craft we're hiring you for.

What we need back, and the bar for each:
- A clean VECTOR MASTER of the mark as an SVG: perfectly upright, the aged-paper look gone, edges crisp, no paper texture, speckle, surface grain or scanner artefacts carried into the paths, and the lettering and icon reading as solid, closed shapes with their counters (the holes in R, O, Q, A) intact. This is our one-colour / K100 master for laser etching and single-colour print, so it has to stay clean and lightweight when a vendor opens the file, not merely look right in a thumbnail.
- The hex-bolt / torque-arrow ICON on its own as a separate clean SVG, for favicons and tiny etched labels where the full wordmark won't fit — the same crisp, closed-path quality as the master, with no stray letterform fragments.
- A REVERSE (white) version of the full lockup on a transparent background, for our dark-anodized plates and dark tool cases: the mark in white, the field genuinely transparent, not sitting on a white box.
- Two SIZED LOCKUPS of the full mark as transparent PNGs — a large one about 2400 px wide for the machine nameplate and a small one about 800 px wide for the screen-printed case label. Both must stay crisp and legible at their size and must not be blown up past what the source actually holds.
- A clean CATALOG PRODUCT SHOT of the physical nameplate itself — the actual metal plate evened out and lifted so it reads as a proper product photo, with the machine, fixings and background gone and the plate sitting on clean white — for the 'made in-house' page of our site.

Finally, hand us a short production note: per file, tell us what you decided to do with it and why, the settings you applied, and the final output sizes — so our production manager can trust the master was rebuilt cleanly and deliberately, not just pushed through an automatic trace.

inputs.name: torqex_artwork_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal flatbed-scanner scan of an old PRINTED logo artwork proof on paper: a bold condensed geometric industrial wordmark reading 'TORQEX' in solid black ink, a compact hex-bolt / torque-arrow icon to its left, and a small 'HYDRAULIC TORQUE SYSTEMS' tagline in caps beneath the wordmark, all flat high-contrast BLACK line art printed on slightly aged off-white / cream paper stock. The whole sheet sits a few degrees crooked on the scanner bed (rotated about 3-4 degrees). Visible signs it is a scan of old paper: faint paper grain and fibre texture, a slightly yellowed/cream cast, a soft grey edge shadow along one side from the scanner lid, a couple of very faint speckles of foxing on the paper margin — but the printed mark itself is crisp, solid, unbroken black. Generous paper margin around the mark. No colour anywhere except black ink on cream paper. Captured at high scanner resolution, long edge about 4200 px.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRACE SOURCE and one half of the triage. Flat, high-contrast, single-ink printed line art is exactly what image_vectorize traces cleanly — but ONLY after prep: the ~3-4deg skew needs image_auto_straighten, the cream cast + paper grain + edge shadow + foxing speckle must be driven out with a tone pass (paper up to clean white, ink to solid black) or the trace will pick them up as stray paths, the generous margin needs crop_to_bounds, and the paper must be knocked to transparency before tracing. Declared at ~4200 px scan scale so the 2400/800 px lockups and reverse are honest DOWNSCALES, never upscales. Superficially it 'is the logo' just like the plate photo — the agent must recognise THIS is the one to rebuild into vector.

inputs.name: torqex_plate_photo.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal DSLR photograph of a rectangular anodized-aluminium machine NAMEPLATE bolted onto industrial equipment, with the 'TORQEX' wordmark, the hex-bolt / torque-arrow icon and a 'HYDRAULIC TORQUE SYSTEMS' tagline LASER-ETCHED into the brushed-metal surface (the etched marks read slightly lighter than the dark-grey anodized field). The plate is shot at a slight three-quarter angle so it is mildly keystoned, not perfectly flat-on. Real photographic conditions: a brushed-metal directional grain across the whole plate, a hot specular glare streak across one corner, four countersunk hex fixing screws at the corners, and out-of-focus machine housing, cabling and a painted equipment panel visible around and behind the plate. Warm-ish workshop lighting, mild uneven exposure across the plate. Real metal, real depth of field, not flat CGI. Long edge about 4500 px.
inputs.realism_notes: THE DECOY / other half of the triage — a PHOTOGRAPH OF METAL, not artwork. It carries the same mark so it looks like 'the logo', but tracing it is the trap: the brushed-metal grain, glare streak, keystone and screws turn into thousands of junk vector paths. Its CORRECT treatment is the opposite branch — tone it into a clean even product shot, crop to the plate, and remove_background to isolate the physical nameplate as a catalog product cutout on white. Declared at ~4500 px camera scale so the cutout downscale is honest. Isolating a rectangular plate from a busy machine background (screws, cabling, housing) is a genuinely harder-than-it-looks cutout.

outputs.name: torqex_master.svg
outputs.spec: The primary deliverable: a clean vector master of the full TORQEX lockup (wordmark + hex-bolt icon + tagline), traced from the PREPPED flat artwork scan — deskewed, aged paper driven to clean white and ink to solid black, cropped to bounds, background knocked to transparency, THEN vectorized. This is the one-colour / K100 master for laser etching and single-colour print. Acceptance (grader-checked): traced from the scan and NOT from the metal photo; upright; solid closed letter/icon shapes with counters (the holes in R, O, Q, A) preserved; no stray paths from paper texture, scanner speckle, edge shadow or the aged cast; path/anchor count in a sane range for a clean wordmark-plus-icon, not the thousands a metal-grain trace would yield.

outputs.name: torqex_bolticon.svg
outputs.spec: The hex-bolt / torque-arrow ICON alone as a separate clean SVG, for favicons and tiny etched labels. Produced by prompt-aware cropping the icon region out of the clean transparent rebuilt mark, trimming it to its own bounds, and vectorizing that — so it carries ONLY the icon, no wordmark or tagline fragments, and the same crisp closed paths as the master. Acceptance: icon-only (no letterforms present), clean paths, traced from the prepped mark not the raw scan or the photo.

outputs.name: torqex_reverse_white.png
outputs.spec: The REVERSE variant: the full TORQEX lockup as flat WHITE art on a fully transparent background, for dark-anodized plates and dark tool cases. Produced by a whole-image white color overlay applied to the mark AFTER it has been knocked to a transparent background, so only the mark's own pixels recolor to white and the field stays transparent. Acceptance: mark is white, background is transparent (not a white rectangle), same lockup geometry as the master.

outputs.name: torqex_plate_lockup_2400.png
outputs.spec: Large sized lockup of the full mark (black on transparent) for the machine nameplate, ~2400 px wide, an honest downscale of the clean rebuilt transparent mark. Acceptance: exact target width, transparent background, no upscaling beyond the ~4200 px scan source.

outputs.name: torqex_label_lockup_800.png
outputs.spec: Small sized lockup of the full mark (black on transparent) for the screen-printed tool-case label, ~800 px wide, downscaled from the same clean rebuilt transparent mark. Acceptance: exact target width, transparent background, still legible at small size, honest downscale.

outputs.name: torqex_plate_product_cutout.png
outputs.spec: From the nameplate PHOTO (NOT the scan, and NEVER vectorized): a clean catalog product cutout of the physical anodized nameplate, evened out and lifted so it reads as a proper product shot, cropped to the plate, with the machine housing, cabling, background and surrounding clutter removed and the plate sitting on solid white. Acceptance: the physical plate is isolated on clean white, machine background gone, and this file is a RASTER photo (the metal photo was isolated, not traced).

outputs.name: torqex_production_notes.txt
outputs.spec: A short production note the agent authors and returns (no measurement, applied settings only): per input, the TREATMENT DECISION and why (which capture was rebuilt into vector vs which was isolated into a product cutout, and the reason the metal photo was not traced), plus the deskew angle, the tone settings and the crop dialed on the scan prep, and the output pixel sizes of the lockups. This is the acceptance artifact that makes the triage decision and the prep auditable rather than eyeballed.

connector_workflow.note: Load the two look-alike captures — the flat printed-artwork scan and the machine-nameplate photo — into the working project in one batch so both triage branches have real asset references. Single upload, plumbing only, not the difficulty.

TRIAGE DECISION made here: the flat printed-artwork scan (torqex_artwork_scan.png) is the trace source, so it enters the prep-before-trace chain. Deskew its ~3-4deg scanner crookedness so the rebuilt vector master is upright and the letter/icon edges trace true. The metal photo does NOT enter this chain — it is handled separately at steps 13-15. Consumes the uploaded scan.

Prep-before-trace tone pass on the deskewed scan: drive the aged cream paper and its faint grain/foxing speckle and edge shadow UP to clean white (whites/highlights up, warm cream cast neutralised) and push the printed ink DOWN to solid black (blacks/contrast up, clarity up to crisp the edges). Goal is a two-value black-on-white mark so the later trace picks up ONLY the mark, not paper texture. Authored from primitives by eye toward a clean-line-art target; NOT auto_tone, NOT a preset. Consumes step 2.

Trim the generous paper margin down to the mark's own tight bounds so the vectorize step spends its resolution on the lettering and icon, not empty paper, and so no margin speckle survives at the edges. Prep-before-trace discipline. Consumes step 3.

Knock the now-clean white paper field to transparency, leaving the solid black mark on a transparent background. This is the clean rebuilt mono mark that every downstream deliverable is derived from (master trace, icon, reverse, sized lockups). White drop-out to transparency, no reconstruction. Consumes step 4.

Trace the fully-prepped transparent mono mark (deskewed, toned to two-value, trimmed, knocked to transparency) into the clean vector master — the one-colour / K100 lockup. Because the raster is prepped, the trace yields solid closed letter/icon shapes with counters preserved and no paper-texture junk paths. DELIVERABLE torqex_master.svg. This is the trace of the SCAN, never the metal photo. Consumes step 5.

Prompt-aware crop of 'the hex-bolt / torque-arrow icon' region out of the clean transparent rebuilt mark, so the icon can be delivered as its own vector without the wordmark. Cropping the icon off the PREPPED mark (not the raw scan or the photo) keeps it clean. Downscale/reframe of existing pixels only. Consumes step 5.
Trim the cropped icon to its own tight bounds so the icon vectorize traces only the glyph — prep-before-trace again, at the icon scale. Consumes step 7.
Vectorize the trimmed icon-only raster into a clean standalone SVG for favicons and tiny etched labels. DELIVERABLE torqex_bolticon.svg — icon only, no letterforms. Consumes step 8.

Produce the REVERSE (white) lockup for dark plates. Constraint-reasoning: image_apply_color_overlay is a WHOLE-IMAGE recolor with no mask — which is exactly right HERE because the input mark has already been knocked to a transparent background, so a whole-image white overlay recolors only the mark's own opaque pixels to white and leaves the field transparent. Applying this overlay BEFORE the background was removed (or trying a masked/selective recolor) is the wrong path; knocking to transparency first is what makes the whole-image tool correct. DELIVERABLE torqex_reverse_white.png (white mark on transparent). Consumes step 5.

Downscale the clean transparent rebuilt mark to the ~2400 px-wide large plate lockup for the machine nameplate. Honest downscale from the ~4200 px scan source, transparent background kept, never enlarged. DELIVERABLE torqex_plate_lockup_2400.png. Consumes step 5.

Downscale the same clean transparent mark to the ~800 px-wide small label lockup for the screen-printed tool case. Honest downscale, transparent background. DELIVERABLE torqex_label_lockup_800.png. Consumes step 5 (cut from the full-res mark, not from the 2400 px file, so the small size is a clean independent downscale).

OTHER TRIAGE BRANCH — the machine-nameplate PHOTO (torqex_plate_photo.jpg), treated as a photo of metal, NOT as artwork. Even out its mild uneven exposure, tame the specular glare streak, and lift/neutralise the warm workshop cast so the anodized plate reads as a clean, evenly-lit catalog product shot. This is a photo grade, never a trace. Consumes the uploaded plate photo.

Prompt-aware crop to 'the rectangular anodized nameplate' so the frame tightens onto the physical plate and drops most of the surrounding machine housing and cabling. Downscale/reframe of the ~4500 px photo, no upscale. Consumes step 13.

Isolate the physical nameplate as a catalog product cutout via remove_background with a solid white backgroundColor — the correct isolation path for lifting the plate off the busy machine background (screws/housing/cabling), NOT a select->invert->fill (which would brick any recessed detail and mis-handle the plate edge). The result is a RASTER product photo of the metal plate on clean white. DELIVERABLE torqex_plate_product_cutout.png — proving the metal photo was isolated, not vectorized. Consumes step 14.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) feeds two triage branches that must be treated OPPOSITELY. TRACE BRANCH (the flat printed-artwork scan -> vector master + all derivatives): auto_straighten (2, deskew) -> image_apply_adjustments (3, two-value tone: paper to white, ink to solid black) -> crop_to_bounds (4, trim margin) -> remove_background (5, knock paper to transparency = the clean rebuilt mono mark) -> vectorize (6, torqex_master.svg). From that clean mark_transparent (step 5) four derivatives fan out: the icon vector via crop_and_resize(7, prompt-crop the icon) -> crop_to_bounds(8, trim) -> vectorize(9, torqex_bolticon.svg); the reverse via image_apply_color_overlay(10, whole-image white on the already-transparent mark = torqex_reverse_white.png); and the two sized lockups via crop_and_resize(11, ~2400 px plate) and crop_and_resize(12, ~800 px label), each an independent downscale from the full-res mark. ISOLATE BRANCH (the machine-nameplate photo -> product cutout, NEVER traced): image_apply_adjustments(13, even the exposure/glare/cast into a clean product grade) -> crop_and_resize(14, prompt-crop to the plate) -> remove_background(15, isolate the plate on solid white = torqex_plate_product_cutout.png). Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; the two branches never cross (the metal photo never enters the vectorize path, the scan never enters the product-cutout path). 15 calls, 8 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon vectorize_logo rebuild scoped to the connector-doable core of the source brief (rebuild a lost mark into a clean scalable vector master plus the one-colour / reverse variants and sized lockups it asks for). Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth: 15 dependent connector calls, 8 distinct Adobe tools, with the whole job hinging on a correct TRIAGE decision — of two captures that both look like 'the logo', only the flat printed-artwork scan may be traced, while the metal-nameplate photo must be isolated into a product cutout and never traced. The trace branch is a strict prep-before-trace chain (deskew -> two-value tone -> crop-to-bounds -> knock-to-transparency -> vectorize) where skipping or reordering any step visibly corrupts the master (a raw-scan trace carries paper grain, foxing speckle and the edge shadow into stray paths; an un-deskewed trace is crooked; an un-toned trace fills counters or breaks strokes). Off the one clean rebuilt mark it derives four different artifacts that each need their own reasoning: an icon-only vector (prompt-crop + re-trim + re-trace, NOT feeding a whole-lockup selection to vectorize), a reverse white lockup that is only correct because the background was knocked to transparency BEFORE the whole-image color overlay, and two honest downscales sized for plate vs label. The parallel isolate branch is its own three-step photo job (even the metal, crop to the plate, remove_background off a cluttered machine). It respects every hard limit: NOTHING is drawn or generated; image_vectorize traces a PREPPED raster (never a raw selection, never the metal photo); the reverse uses whole-image color_overlay on an already-transparent mono mark (its correct whole-image use, not a masked photo recolor); isolation uses remove_background({backgroundColor}) not select->invert->fill; every raster output is an honest downscale from a declared camera/scanner-scale source; no generative fill/expand, no upscaling, no compositing, no from-scratch letterform design, no measurement/eyedropper. The owned endpoint is an agent-rebuilt vector master and production set whose cleanliness is the agent's decision, not a template's.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): the agent is handed two captures that both read as 'the TORQEX logo' and must triage them to OPPOSITE treatments — prep-and-trace the flat printed-artwork scan into the vector master, but isolate (never trace) the photograph of the etched metal nameplate. Trace the wrong capture, or trace the scan raw without the deskew/tone/crop/knock-to-transparency prep, and the 'vector master' is visibly broken (a crooked mark, filled-in counters, or thousands of brushed-metal / paper-texture junk paths) — invisible from a thumbnail, obvious the moment the SVG is opened. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) the triage itself — two superficially identical inputs needing different correct pipelines, where getting it wrong is silent until inspected; (2) prep-before-trace discipline on the scan — deskew, then a two-value tone that drives aged cream paper and speckle to clean white and ink to solid black, then crop-to-bounds, then knock-to-transparency, all BEFORE vectorize, or the trace is dirty; (3) constraint-reasoning around tool limits — the reverse white lockup is only clean because the mark was knocked to transparency FIRST so a whole-image color overlay hits only the mark (not select->invert->fill, not a masked photo recolor), the icon is pulled by prompt-crop + re-trim + re-trace (not by feeding a selection to vectorize, which returns a silhouette), and the plate is isolated with remove_background({backgroundColor}) off a cluttered machine. TRAP: the naive 'vectorize the logo' path — trace whichever picture looks like the logo, or trace the raw un-prepped scan — looks right and fails, because a trace of photographed brushed aluminium (or of an aged paper scan) explodes into junk paths that still resemble the mark at a glance. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, agent never measures): torqex_master.svg is traced from the SCAN (not the metal photo), upright, with solid closed letters/icon and preserved counters and a sane path/anchor count rather than thousands of texture paths; torqex_bolticon.svg contains the icon only, no letterforms; torqex_reverse_white.png is white-on-transparent (not a white rectangle); the two lockups hit their exact widths as honest downscales of the ~4200 px scan; torqex_plate_product_cutout.png is a RASTER photo of the isolated plate on white (proving the metal photo was isolated, not traced); and the returned production note states the per-file treatment decision and the applied deskew/tone/crop/size settings.
